pending: 1. BUG (HIGH — the user hit it live, 13k console errors): the LoRA & Upscale button opens MpiModelSettings in a REOPEN LOOP that cannot be closed. User repro: click LoRA & Upscale in the model picker -> nothing appears (it opens UNDER the picker overlay); close the picker -> Model Settings is there; click its X -> it flashes and pops straight back. Console fills with `net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` on GET /comfy/model-folders + POST /log, traced to `_renderDropZones (MpiModelSettings.js:287)` called from `el.open (MpiModelSettings.js:601)`. DIAGNOSIS (read, not yet proven by instrumentation): `el.open()` awaits `loadAssets()` = `assetService.loadAll()`, which ALWAYS assigns fresh arrays to `state.availableLoras` AND `state.upscaleModels` (js/services/assetService.js:27-28) — the state Proxy fires `state:changed` on every assign, identical content or not. MpiModelSettings' live-rerender subscription (MpiModelSettings.js:249-252) answers `state:changed` for exactly those two keys with `el.open(_context)`. So open-while-already-open re-enters open, and each pass fires TWO state:changed events => exponential fan-out, which is why the error count explodes. The FIRST open is safe only by accident: `_isOpen = true` is set at line 613, AFTER the await, so the initial pass fails the `if (!_isOpen ...)` guard — that ordering is load-bearing today and is not documented. Fix the cause (a re-entrancy guard on open, or make loadAll only assign when the list content actually changed, or have the listener rebuild the dropdowns without re-running open), NOT by removing the live-rerender feature. Also check the z-order half: the settings overlay opened from the picker renders UNDER the picker (Overlays stack), which is why the first click looked like a no-op.

Use `el.setOperation(op, { programmatic: true })` so it does NOT poison `s_selectedOpByModel` — step 8's memory is what restores the user's real op when media comes back, and a non-programmatic write here would erase it.

key_decisions: USER DECISION: `inpaint` needs NO prompt. Empty prompt = erase the masked area and fill from the surroundings; with a prompt = replace it. That is why one op replaces both `change` and `remove`, and why `promptRequired: false` is load-bearing (a test pins it).
USER DECISION: `change` and `remove` are deprecated, `edit` STAYS (the user corrected an earlier slip — `edit` is Boogu Image Edit's only op, both tiers).
USER DECISION: the popup's op strip goes at the BOTTOM, not the top — the popup grows upward from the cogwheel, so a top strip jumps out from under the cursor on every pick.

USER DECISION (reversal): the cogwheel should go BACK after the model selector and look like the other bar buttons. The user's original reason for moving it first (it looked different) is better solved by restyling it.
The op strip has TWO mounts of ONE choice list (bar + popup). They cannot disagree: `_refreshOpStrip` rebuilds both and both emit the same `workspace:set-operation`, which the owning Block validates.

The capture-phase click record on popupNode is not a nicety — without it the popup closes on every in-popup op change, because the clicked button is detached by its own handler before the document dismiss runs.
Ops left the radial entirely. `navigation.RADIAL_ITEMS` is one static item (Models); Apps pushes the second and the ring comes back with no further edit.
